stem: Who is the patron saint of Scotland?
explanation: St Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland and St Andrew's Day is 30 November. St David is for Wales, St George for England and St Patrick for Northern Ireland.

stem: When is St David's Day, the national day of Wales?
explanation: St David's Day is on 1 March. St Patrick's Day is 17 March, St George's Day is 23 April and St Andrew's Day is 30 November.

stem: When is St George's Day?
explanation: St George is the patron saint of England and his day is 23 April.

stem: Who is the head of the Church of England?
explanation: The monarch is the head of the Church of England. The Archbishop of Canterbury is its spiritual leader.

stem: People in the UK are free to choose any religion, or to have no religion.
explanation: The UK has religious freedom. People can follow any faith, change their faith or have none.

stem: What is the national church in Scotland?
explanation: The Church of Scotland is a Presbyterian church. It is run by ministers and elders, not by the monarch.

stem: Which Christian group is governed by a General Assembly and a Moderator?
explanation: The Church of Scotland is a Presbyterian church. It is led by the Moderator of the General Assembly, who serves for one year.

stem: The Church in Wales and the Church of Ireland are 'established' churches like the Church of England.
explanation: Only the Church of England and the Church of Scotland are established churches. This means they have a special legal link with the state.

stem: Who was the founder of the Methodist Church in the 18th century?
explanation: John Wesley founded the Methodist Church to reach people who did not attend the Church of England. It is now one of the largest 'Free Churches' in the UK.

stem: Which religious group is also known as the 'Religious Society of Friends'?
explanation: The Quakers were founded by George Fox in the 17th century. They are known for their commitment to peace and simple living.

stem: Which TWO of the following are examples of 'Free Churches' in the UK?
explanation: Free Churches are Christian groups that are not part of the established Church of England. Other examples include the United Reformed Church.

stem: Who started the Salvation Army in the 19th century to help the poor?
explanation: The Salvation Army is a Christian group that focuses on social work. It works in many countries to provide food and shelter to people in need.

stem: The United Kingdom is a secular society, which means that religious ideas do not govern the laws of the country.
explanation: Although there are established churches, the UK is a secular society. This means everyone is free to practice any religion or none at all.

stem: What is another name for the Church of England?
explanation: The Church of England is often called the Anglican Church. In other countries, churches with similar beliefs are part of the Anglican Communion.

stem: How long does the Moderator of the General Assembly of the Church of Scotland serve for?
explanation: The Moderator is the head of the Church of Scotland for a 12-month period. They represent the church at official events.

stem: Which religious leader is the spiritual head of the Roman Catholic Church?
explanation: The Roman Catholic Church has millions of members in the UK. Its worldwide leader is the Pope, who is based in the Vatican.

stem: Which TWO of the following statements about the Church of England are true?

options.label: It is the established church in England.
The Monarch is the head of the church.
It has no links to the state.

explanation: The Church of England was established during the Reformation. The King or Queen holds the title 'Defender of the Faith' as its head.

stem: People in the UK are allowed to change their religion at any time.
explanation: Freedom of religion is a key part of life in the UK. People can choose their own faith, change it, or have no religion at all.

stem: Which church in the UK is a Presbyterian church?
explanation: The Church of Scotland is a Presbyterian church, which means it is governed by elders. It is one of the two established churches in the UK.

stem: Who has the right to appoint the Archbishop of Canterbury?
explanation: The Monarch is the head of the Church of England. They appoint senior church leaders on the advice of the Prime Minister.

stem: Which Christian group grew quickly in the 18th century by preaching in the streets to working people?
explanation: Methodism began as a movement within the Church of England. John Wesley and others travelled around the country to reach people who did not go to church.

stem: How many senior bishops of the Church of England sit in the House of Lords?
explanation: There are 26 senior Church of England bishops who have seats in the House of Lords. This shows the church's role as the official state religion in England.

stem: The British monarch has the official title ‘Defender of the Faith’.
explanation: The monarch is the head of the Church of England and uses the title 'Defender of the Faith'. This title has been used by monarchs for hundreds of years.

stem: In the UK census, which of these is the largest religious group after Christians?
explanation: According to census data, Islam is the second largest religion in the UK. There are also many people who say they have no religion at all.

stem: Which TWO of these major religions have many followers in the UK today?
explanation: The UK is home to people from many faiths. Hinduism and Judaism are two of the largest non-Christian religious groups in the country.

stem: Which of these statements about the monarch and the Church of Scotland is true?

options.label: The monarch is a member but not the head
The monarch is the supreme governor
The monarch chooses the church leaders
The monarch is not allowed to join

explanation: The Church of Scotland is a Presbyterian church and is independent. The monarch is a member of the church but does not lead it.
